verdict.rationale: React's docs say adding @types/react and @types/react-dom gives full React Web TypeScript support, and the editor-setup page recommends eslint-plugin-react-hooks rules that catch bugs early. This implies typed editor tooling through the standard TypeScript and ESLint ecosystems rather than a React-owned language service. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of editor autocompletion and inline type-error diagnostics, any first-party language service or editor integration, and independent or hands-on corroboration of editor DX quality.
